steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Given I'm here, all of you can come out now.

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: Lieutenant.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: How are my people?

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: Your subordinates are here. Rest assured, they're only unconscious.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I don't mean Cello's group.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You know who I mean.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Don't push me, or it won't be my shield against your chin.

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: *Cough*, *cough* *cough*... If you're going to draw your sword, you'll be attacking a colleague...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Heh. Colleague?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: At what point, since the moment we entered County Hillock, have you ever treated us as colleagues?!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Answer me!!!

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: Hff—

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: Even supposing... you... cut my throat here... you can't alter... the Colonel's decision...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You've never heard the degree of what the Tempest Platoon's soldiers can do, have you?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: How many did Triangle cost you? Half your own company?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It's just me alone here. But I guarantee you, you won't want to know how long it takes me to put you all to rights.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: L—Lay down your weapons!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Or else, w... we'll kill her on the spot!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...Cello.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: I mean it! Make one move, and my crossbow's shooting straight through her neck!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You win.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Subdue her! Quickly, together now, we can't let her touch her sword and shield again!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Hill... you tell Hamilton...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Victoria is ashamed of him.

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: The Colonel has no need whatsoever for Victoria's gratitude.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Got the data all nice and pretty?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: Yes, Lass, it's all in here.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Wonderful.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I see Oliver's all done with the comms too.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Collaborating businesses have received notice. As per the agreement clauses, they can either seek an office in another city nearby, or terminate the contract.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: *Sigh*. Looking at it, these aren't losses for us to sneeze at.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Rhodes Island isn't the only company taking a hit in the chaos of war.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: True, no way around that. I just look at the chairs and tables in here and there's a twinge in my heart. This place of ours was still empty, back when I first came to County Hillock.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: A little early for separation anxiety, Oliver. How do you know we won't be right back, huh?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: You're right. *Sigh*. I hope this city can return to the old peaceful everydays soon enough.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Storehouse medications, inventory finished.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I need you to ration out these meds. Each one of you needs to bring enough emergency medication, make sure everyone makes it smoothly to the closest branch office.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: There's still a lot left over, sharing like that.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: There'll be some pressure if we take it all. We don't have that many hands, after all.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Shredder's quiet as ever, but I can tell, you have your own ideas.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: The people in the city... They need medicines.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Turns out I think so too. If this war scales up, everything's gonna be in short supply, especially Oripathy painkillers and suppressants that need to be taken long-term.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You must have a list of hospitals in the area?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Already sorted.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Think of a way to get it to them. No matter who these organizations serve, get as much as you can to all of them.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And don't forget the little alley clinics. Plenty of them out there without signs, but a lot of our friends around here rely on them.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Lass, is this really proper? We never bypass local healthcare, directly providing medical organizations and individuals with pharmaceuticals.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Desperate times call for desperate measures. And it's not like a hospital's gonna refuse an 'anonymous donation' from concerned citizens, right?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: True! So you got it all figured out, eh. But then, who'll take charge of sending it? The people around all know we're Rhodes Islanders.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I will... I can help Shredder parcel the medicine, and then I'll deliver it.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Jane, you all better?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: My wounds aren't bleeding anymore.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You know I'm not asking about the wounds.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I didn't want to be tucked alone in a corner crying while you were all bustling about.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'm glad you can help, but we've got a lot of meds here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Please, trust a Vouivre's stamina.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I just don't want Rhodes Island work getting in the way of your own plans.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's alright. From here to the zone of battle, there just so happens to be plenty of hospitals and clinics along the way.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Once I'm done delivering, I'll rejoin you.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Just a little left. We'll be done with wrapping in no time.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Then it's about time we got on our way.
As Outcast speaks, she draws a revolver from the holster at her side.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Whoa. That's your gun?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That it is.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: For a Sankta, pre-op prep's only complete once your gun's loaded.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: It doesn't look like your chamber's full.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Under normal circumstances, five rounds is enough to do the trick.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: When I was back at the landship and ate with Barty's group, I heard a lot of stories from the field about you.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: You once took down three Columbian bandits with a single bullet, and used three to scatter a whole mercenary team.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: If I had to guess, there wouldn't be an enemy out there worth six straight shots?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Can't say for sure. After all, there's always a bigger beast.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: But I made a promise to someone that I'd never fire a sixth round lightly—because we made a bet.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I can't help but be curious. What kind of bet would make someone like you change up how you work?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That's a long story.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: The short version is that friend of mine tried every way under the sun to show me an easy retirement.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And I always had a feeling that even if I retired for real, someone like me just couldn't live peaceful.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Like right now?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I never imagined County Hillock could turn so restless. It was just a day or two ago, we were all huddled together playing cards and drinking tea...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: A lot of times, a situation's like the color of the sky, shifting on and on.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: If it's up to me, I'd sure like this retreat operation to go nice and quiet-like. Best case scenario, I don't even need to fire one round.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: ...Lass, it's all ready.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Friends, it's time to say goodbye.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Janie...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You don't need to be so sad, Uncle Oliver. I trust in what Outcast says—we can surely see each other again!

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Jane, be careful.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I will, Shredder. All of you too, be sure to take care of yourselves.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Oh... did I hear thunder?

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: ...It'll be raining soon enough.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: No. Something's not right about that sound. Jane, stay inside for now!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Mr. Chef, Mr. Chef, are you here?!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Agh! Yes, I'm here, I'm here! Stop it with the banging! There's too much lampblack on our office door. Can't stand up to knocks.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Okay, good, you're still here... here's the thing, I need a Messenger, we've got important information that needs sendin' out!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Yeah, I understand. Fancy that, I've got something to give to you too.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? What's this? A piece of... paper?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: It's a list of stationed officers—the one named Louis Kelly, he just handed it to me.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Captain Kelly? How'd he get in touch with you?

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Relax, he's got no clue who I am. It was only 'cause I was the last person he ran into.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: I was going to go poking around for the latest. Still remember my actual job, after all... Didn't imagine I'd run into the troops arresting him!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Arrestin'... him? You mean, Captain Kelly's been arrested by his own?!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: They said he was harboring Oripathics! But that can't be right. His son passed from Oripathy a few months ago, the whole city knows that. The first thing he did was report the news his son'd gotten ill!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: These people... usin' such a tragic illness as an excuse? That's beyond shameless!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Not just once or twice, either. For people wanting to use any form of discrimination as a front, it's true, Oripathy is an especially good pretense.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Just take this time. The troops are weeding out any inside people born Taran.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Officers or soldiers, so long as they were kindred with Tarans in some way, were stripped overnight of any right to act freely.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Clearin' out the barracks' Tarans? In wartime, pressed for people? I've got an awful feelin' about this already.

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: So, Captain Kelly slipped me this like his life depended on it, wanted me to give it to 'the soldier not from this barracks who's constantly been hanging around here as of late'—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Mr. Chef, this is proof the barracks are makin' illegal Originium weapons!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: What?! Hamilton's lost his mind!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I want you to find a trustworthy Messenger, give 'em this paper and our report about the spectre force both, to be treated as vital intelligence, and taken out of County Hillock straight away!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: This is the Captain's endeavor in his final moment! We cannot waste it!

steps.name: Chef MacMartin
steps.text: Can't do that. This information's too important, and we can't rely on a civilian Messenger. How about this instead, Miss—I'll make this trip myself.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Mr. Chef, you were a Messenger too?

steps.name: Messenger MacMartin
steps.text: Don't forget, passing on information's part of us lamplighters' profession too. Ah, finally, I can take on a decent assignment at long last. Excitement's got my hands and legs shaking.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Wait, hold on, there's some sound outside...

steps.name: Messenger MacMartin
steps.text: It's lightning, isn't it?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'm feelin' doubtful about that.

steps.name: Messenger MacMartin
steps.text: It's fine, I've been here in County Hillock how many years now. The weather changes when it wants to. Used to it at this point.

steps.name: Messenger MacMartin
steps.text: A little lightning and rain can't hold me back! I'm off!

a.text: The Messenger charges into the recess of the street with nary a look back.
On his head, a hard rain is pouring down, and the thunder gradually nears, getting concentrated, louder—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: This... this isn't lightning!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No, Mr. Chef—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: —This is bombardment!!!

a.text: The Messenger isn't in time to hear her words.
Countless shells come down with the rain, exploding the moment they contact the ground and walls.

The blast waves tear effortlessly through the gel material, blisteringly and ferociously melting the metal makeup, but the more fearsome thing takes advantage of the illness that bores beneath the city's muscle and bone—

Incomplete combustion sees immense formations of Originium crystal, solidifying dense within the open wounds of streets and buildings, as if in the dirty rain, identically and rapidly, bloom pure black flowers.
